The hypothesis is grounded in S2 oxidative residual metabolism and S4 DHODH-inhibition differentiation, while correctly flagging atovaquone, complex III inhibition, ubiquinone dependence and salvage limitation as unverified. It provides a coherent pyrimidine-depletion mechanism with uridine and respiratory-chain-independent DHODH rescue tests and a falsifier, but it is less detailed than the parallel proposal about timing, exposure thresholds, and selectivity gates.

The causal design is unusually explicit: pre-specified eligibility, ATP-sparing time gate, enzyme selectivity, and uridine/URA1 rescue with teriflunomide validation distinguish DHODH-dependent differentiation from ATP collapse or direct DHODH inhibition. Several numeric gates are not derived from the packet, and the many sequential primary-specimen, engineered-line, and xenograft steps make feasibility lower.

The proposal uses S2 and S4 to motivate oxidative residual AML and DHODH-linked differentiation, but it explicitly labels the key atovaquone, complex III, ubiquinone-DHODH, uridine-bypass and protein-binding claims as unverified prior knowledge. Its causal chain is unusually well ordered and it specifies prespecified gates, rescue epistasis, enzyme assays, free-drug exposure limits and a clear falsifying outcome, though the unbound-exposure window and normal-progenitor selectivity remain major translational risks.

The central kinase/site claim remains unsupported by S1-S4, and the primary-neuron phosphoproteomics and knock-in strategy are ambitious, reducing feasibility.

The hypothesis is scoped to TDP-43 proteinopathy and cites S1-S4 appropriately. Kinase, sites, and direction remain unsupported assumptions, and phosphomimetic Asp/Glu interpretation is a weakness. Temporal and perturbational tests are reasonable, but iPSC plus in vivo endpoints are resource-intensive.

Most rigorous version: validates modification before causal claims, uses MS site mapping, inducible kinase recruitment instead of relying on Asp/Glu mimics, reconstituted permeabilized neurons, pulse-washout, and graded predictions at matched SG burden; central kinase/site/direction assumptions remain.

Strong use of S1-S4 with explicit assumptions and downstream decoupling of Ran, stress granules, and TDP-43 assemblies. Causal discrimination is unusually rigorous: MS validation, phospho-null panel, graded predictions, and clear falsification. The digitonin reconstitution and staged in vivo arm lower feasibility, but the design is testable and highly specified.
